description: LRUCache evicts the wrong key because get() and put() on existing keys do not refresh recency; fix the eviction order.
prompt:
You are fixing an LRU cache bug in JavaScript.

File: work/swe-06/lru.js

The exported class `LRUCache` (constructor takes `capacity`) supports `put(key, value)` and `get(key)` (returns the value, or `-1` on miss), evicting the least-recently-used key when over capacity. Currently `get()` and `put()` on an existing key do NOT refresh recency, so the wrong key gets evicted.

Example of the bug: with capacity 2, `put(1,1); put(2,2); get(1); put(3,3)` should evict `2` (least recently used), but the buggy version evicts `1`.

Requirements:
- `get()` on a hit must mark the key most-recently-used; misses return `-1` with no side effects.
- `put()` on an existing key must update the value AND mark it most-recently-used.
- `put()` on a new key when full must evict exactly the least-recently-used key (capacity 1 must work).
- Keep `module.exports = { LRUCache }` and use no external dependencies.

Edit work/swe-06/lru.js so the behavior above holds.
title: Fix LRU cache eviction order
